paper_metadata.title: NCERT Class 7 Science Chapter 10 Model Test Paper
instructions: Section A contains 6 Objective Questions (4 MCQs + 2 Assertion-Reason) carrying 1 Mark each.
Section B contains 5 Short Answer Questions carrying 2 Marks each.
Section C contains 2 Long Answer Questions carrying 4 Marks each.
Section D contains 1 Case-Based Competency Question with 3 sub-questions carrying 2 Marks each.

questions.question_text: The vascular tissue responsible for unidirectional water transport in plants is:
questions.marking_scheme: 1 Mark for correct option selection (B). Explanation: Xylem vessels conduct water and dissolved soil minerals unidirectionally from roots to leaves.

questions.question_text: What is the key scientific indicator or property studied in Chapter 10?
questions.marking_scheme: 1 Mark for correct option selection (A). Explanation: Derived from core terms.

questions.question_text: Which process occurs during the core phenomenon in Life Processes in Plants?
questions.marking_scheme: 1 Mark for correct option (C). Explanation: Standard curriculum observation.

questions.question_text: Select the correct definition for 'Photosynthesis Chemical Equation':
questions.marking_scheme: 1 Mark for correct option (A). Explanation: Definition of Photosynthesis Chemical Equation as stated in NCERT textbook.

questions.question_text:
Assertion (A): Plants release oxygen during daytime photosynthesis.
Reason (R): Photosynthetic oxygen production rate exceeds respiration consumption rate during sunlight hours.
options: A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
C) (A) is true but (R) is false.
D) (A) is false but (R) is true.
questions.marking_scheme: 1 Mark for correct selection (A). Explanation: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.question_text:
Assertion (A): Xylem conducts water and minerals unidirectionally upwards.
Reason (R): Transpiration pull creates suction pressure that draws water up xylem vessels.
options: A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
C) (A) is true but (R) is false.
D) (A) is false but (R) is true.
questions.marking_scheme: 1 Mark for correct selection (A). Explanation: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.question_text: How do non-green or dark red leaves perform photosynthesis?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Dark red, purple, or brown leaves still contain chlorophyll. Large quantities of red or brown carotenoid/anthocyanin pigments mask the green color without preventing photosynthesis.
questions.breakdown: 1 Mark for identifying first key point; 1 Mark for second key point / clear explanation.

questions.question_text: Why are green leaves designated as the primary 'food factories' of plants?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Leaves contain green chlorophyll pigment within chloroplasts, which traps solar light energy to combine atmospheric CO2 and root-absorbed water into chemical energy (starch).
questions.breakdown: 1 Mark for statement/formula; 1 Mark for calculation/application.
1 Mark for Point 1 of difference; 1 Mark for Point 2 of difference.

questions.question_text: Why is it dangerous to sleep directly under large trees at night?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: At night, in the absence of sunlight, plants stop photosynthesis (which consumes CO2 and produces O2) but continue cellular respiration (which consumes O2 and releases CO2), increasing local CO2 levels.
questions.breakdown: 1 Mark for identifying core cause; 1 Mark for explaining scientific effect.

questions.question_text: Correct the common misconception: 'Believing plants produce oxygen during both day and night.'. Provide the correct scientific fact.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Plants release oxygen only during daytime when photosynthesis occurs under light. At night, plants consume oxygen for cellular respiration.
questions.breakdown: 1 Mark for identifying error; 1 Mark for stating correct scientific fact.

sections.section_name: Section C (Long Answer Questions - Diagrams & Processes)

questions.question_text: Explain plant nutrition thoroughly: raw materials, stomata structure, photosynthesis chemical equation, starch storage test, and dual vascular transport (Xylem & Phloem).
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Raw Materials: Atmospheric CO2 via leaf stomata, water/minerals via root hair absorption, solar energy trapped by chlorophyll. 2. Photosynthesis: 6CO2 + 6H2O -> C6H12O6 + 6O2. 3. Starch Test: Boiling leaf in alcohol removes green chlorophyll; iodine turns stored starch blue-black. 4. Transport: Xylem transports water/minerals upwards; Phloem translocates synthesized sugars to all plant organs.
questions.breakdown: 1 Mark for introduction/definition; 2 Marks for detailed 4-point mechanism; 1 Mark for conclusion/example.

questions.question_text: Explain the structure and operation illustrated in 'Fig. 10.3 / Microscopic Structure of Stomata'. (i) Draw/describe the key components (Stomatal Pore, Guard Cells (Kidney-shaped), Chloroplasts, Epidermal Cells). (ii) Detail the working mechanism and scientific significance.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Component breakdown: Stomatal Pore, Guard Cells (Kidney-shaped), Chloroplasts, Epidermal Cells.
Mechanism & Significance: Regulates gaseous exchange and transpiration water loss in plant leaves.
questions.breakdown: 2 Marks for labeling/describing key components accurately; 2 Marks for explaining working mechanism clearly.

question.case_scenario_text: A student wraps a transparent plastic bag over a leafy branch of a potted plant placed in sunlight.

sub_questions.question_text: What appears inside the plastic bag after 2 hours, and what biological process does it demonstrate?
sub_questions.marking_scheme_answer: Tiny water droplets collect on the inner surface of the plastic bag, demonstrating Transpiration (loss of water vapor through leaf stomata).
sub_questions.breakdown: 2 Marks for complete, accurate identification/explanation of the initial phenomenon.

sub_questions.question_text: Formulate a testable hypothesis or identify the chemical/physical principle.
sub_questions.breakdown: 2 Marks for correct scientific reasoning and principle formulation.

sub_questions.question_text: What conclusion or practical precaution can be derived from this experimental observation?
sub_questions.marking_scheme_answer: Practical conclusion and safety/precautionary measure grounded in textbook guidelines.
sub_questions.breakdown: 2 Marks for valid evidence-based conclusion / real-world application.
